elements.quote: A MedDiet has been associated with improved metabolic syndrome (MetS) outcomes, including a decreased risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and obesity, among adults. However, the extent to which different levels of adherence to the MedDiet are associated with MetS outcomes in youth remains poorly understood.
elements.reason: The introduction explicitly describes the existing knowledge (benefits in adults) and highlights the key uncertainty (unknown association in children/adolescents).

elements.quote: The prevalence of metabolic disorders is increasing globally, especially among adolescents, and this has become a public health concern... Therefore, the aim of this systematic review and meta‑analysis was to investigate whether adherence to a MedDiet is associated with MetS in this population.
elements.reason: The text explains why the review is needed, linking the growing public‑health burden to the gap in knowledge and stating the review’s purpose.

elements.quote: To our knowledge, no previous systematic review or meta‑analysis has synthesised the available evidence examining the association between adherence to the MedDiet and MetS among children and adolescents.
elements.reason: The authors state that no similar systematic reviews exist, so the conditional requirement to discuss existing reviews does not apply.

elements.quote: Several potential mechanisms may explain the observed association between adherence to the MedDiet and improved MetS. The MedDiet is characterised by a high intake of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds and healthy fats...
elements.reason: Although mechanisms are described, the review is not of an intervention effect; therefore the conditional element concerning intervention mechanisms is not applicable.
No logic model or schematic of hypothesised relationships is presented, and the review does not involve a complex intervention requiring such a model.
No retrieved passage provides an explicit statement of the review objectives or research question, nor does it use a question‑formulation framework such as PICO, PICOS, or similar.

elements.quote: To be eligible for inclusion in the present review, studies needed to meet the following criteria: ... (i) were children or adolescents aged 5-19 years, ... (iv) had a longitudinal and cross‑sectional study design.
elements.reason: The review includes only longitudinal and cross‑sectional observational studies, not intervention trials; therefore a PICO‑style statement of planned comparisons is not relevant.

elements.quote: To be eligible for inclusion in the present review, studies needed to meet the following criteria: (i) were children or adolescents aged 5-19 years, all countries and ethnic backgrounds; (ii) had a MetS outcome; (iii) had an adherence to the MedDiet assessed by a validated questionnaire; and (iv) had a longitudinal and cross- sectional study design.
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria list participant age, setting (all countries/ethnicities), outcome, exposure measurement, and study designs, satisfying most of the required characteristics. No explicit follow‑up duration or requirement is reported, so the element is only partially satisfied.

elements.quote: we restricted our inclusion criteria to studies published in English.
elements.reason: The language restriction for reports is stated, fulfilling part of the requirement. The criterion does not provide the dissemination year or publication status, so the element is only partially met.
No evidence is provided that the review distinguishes exclusions due to outcomes not being measured from exclusions due to outcomes not being reported.
The retrieved text does not specify the groups used in each synthesis nor link them to the review’s comparison objectives.

elements.quote: However, to narrow the scope of the meta- analysis, only studies that associated the MedDiet with the outcome of MetS were included.
elements.reason: A clear rationale is given for the restriction that only studies linking the Mediterranean diet to MetS outcomes were considered, satisfying the conditional element.
